subject.title: [Bug]: Cron isolated agentTurn skips delivery before dispatch when a recovered early tool error is classified as fatal

question: For recovered isolated cron runs where a process-ran exec/tool failure is followed by final assistant output, should cron record success, error, or a degraded/warning outcome, and should completion delivery proceed?
rationale: Current code cannot distinguish all safe recovery cases, and the choice changes persisted cron status, delivery state, alerts, and retry/backoff behavior rather than being a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add degraded cron outcome
options.body: Introduce typed exec phase evidence and a degraded/warning cron state that can still dispatch completion delivery while preserving failure diagnostics and alert semantics.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Continue treating process-ran nonzero failures as fatal until a later explicit same-action recovery contract proves the failure is resolved, accepting missed reports to avoid false success.

options.title: Treat final assistant output as success
options.body: Prefer final assistant visible output after session success for delivery, but this risks hiding unresolved mutating failures without the typed phase and degraded-state work.

recommendation.title: Add degraded cron outcome
recommendation.body: Introduce typed exec phase evidence and a degraded/warning cron state that can still dispatch completion delivery while preserving failure diagnostics and alert semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and already gave the maintainer direction that this needs typed exec phase evidence and degraded cron outcome semantics.
